record.paper_title: Некоторые экстремальные задачи для векторных расслоений
record.original_question: For n≥3, determine the optimal disk diameter D_n with the following property: every continuous field of planar convex figures of diameter at most 1 in γ^n_2 contains a fiber figure that lies in a Euclidean disk of diameter at most D_n. Known bounds in this setting are D_n≤sec(π/(2n+2)) for even n and n=3, and D_n≤sec(π/(2n)) for odd n≥5; the exact value is unknown.

evidence.quote: Следствие. При четном n и n = 3 любое п.в.ф. диаметра ≤ 1 в расслоении γn2 содержит фигуру, лежащую в круге диаметра sec π/(2n+2). При нечетном n ≥ 5 любое п.в.ф. диаметра ≤ 1 в расслоении γn2 содержит фигуру, лежащую в круге диаметра sec π/(2n).
При n ≥ 3 точная оценка диаметра круга автору не известна.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 3 be an integer and let γ^n_2 denote the tautological 2-plane bundle over the real Grassmannian G_2(R^n) of 2-dimensional linear subspaces of R^n; each fiber of γ^n_2 is a Euclidean plane (a 2-dimensional subspace of R^n with the induced inner product). By a continuous field of planar convex figures in γ^n_2 we mean a continuous assignment to each point L ∈ G_2(R^n) of a compact convex subset F(L) ⊂ L (continuity taken with respect to the Hausdorff metric on compact convex sets, after locally trivializing the bundle). Such a field is said to have diameter at most 1 if diam(F(L)) ≤ 1 for every L. 

Define D_n to be the infimum of all real numbers D > 0 with the following property: every continuous field F of planar convex figures of diameter at most 1 in γ^n_2 contains at least one fiber figure F(L_0) that is contained in some Euclidean disk (inside L_0) of diameter at most D.

Determine the exact value of D_n for each n ≥ 3. It is known that
  D_n ≤ sec(π/(2n+2))  for even n and for n = 3,
  D_n ≤ sec(π/(2n))    for odd n ≥ 5.
artifact.status_search_result: No web evidence was found of a sharp determination of D_n. The problem is explicitly stated as unresolved, with only the upper bounds sec(π/(2n+2)) (for even n and n=3) and sec(π/(2n)) (for odd n ≥ 5) known; no subsequent work providing matching lower bounds or the exact value could be located.
